newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, U.S. customs to jointly inspect HK factories.
newsitem.headline: HK, U.S. customs to jointly inspect HK factories.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Monday it would allow United States officials to join its customs officers to inspect textiles factories in the colony next month in a bid to resolve a trade row with Washington.
The visit will be the second by U.S. Customs officers since September.
"If the joint teams confirm that a consignment is of Hong Kong origin, U.S. Customs will lift the single entry bond requirement for the consignment," a government spokesman said in a statement.
"Or if the single entry bond has already been submitted, the U.S. Customs will liquidate the entry and the importer will be relieved of all conditional release obligations," he said.
The United States imposed on June 17 stringent new rules requiring Hong Kong textile exporters to provide additional import documentation on a number of clothing products.
The rules were enacted to prevent illegal trans-shipments passing from China through Hong Kong to avoid quota restrictions on Chinese exports to the United States.
Washington claims that goods from China are avoiding quota limits with false "made in Hong Kong" labels.
